newsitem.title: USA: Ford prices Navigator starting at $39,950.
newsitem.headline: Ford prices Navigator starting at $39,950.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said it will sell its 1998 Lincoln Navigator sport utility vehicle at prices starting at $39,950.

Ford, which made the announcement at the New York Auto show on Wednesday, said suggested retail prices for the Navigator 4x2 model will start at $39,950 and at $43,300 for the 4x4 model, both including destination charges.

The Navigator will be unveiled on July 1, according to Jim O'Connor, Ford Motor Co vice president in charge of Lincoln. Ford said all Navigator models offer an array of standard features and are backed by limited warranty coverage for 48 months or 50,000 miles.
Navigator's suggested retail price positions it favorably against Toyota Motor Corp's Lexus and BMW's Range Rover, O'Connor said.
"Lincoln is a brand in transition and Navigator is a first installment (in this transition)," O'Connor said. "We are reaching a broader base with the Navigator."

Standard features include load-leveling air suspension, a 5.4-liter V-8 engine mated to a 4-speed electronic automatic overdrive transmission and specially developed shocks and tires. Standard safety features include four-wheel disc anti-lock breaks, driver/front passenger air bag supplemental restraint system, side impact door beams and rear door child safety locks.

"We set out to make Navigator the vehicle that redefines the full-size luxury SUV," O'Connor said. Ford's goal was to combine the hallmarkds of a Lincoln - quiet, luxury, smooth ride and sophisticated performance with the attributes of an off-road vehicle at a very competitive price, O'Connor said.
